# Automatic build recovery

The supervisor handles terminal timeout/stall/spawn/worktree failures and diagnostic holds after the runner releases its lock. A fresh Luna xhigh diagnosis feeds a separately authorized coordinator repair scope. Recovered artifacts remain unverified. Repairs run in isolated Git worktrees, pass fixed acceptance and an independent reviewer, then publish a controller receipt and call the supported DAG retry command. Normal task review still determines completion.

Frozen specifications, graph ownership, thresholds, guard code and existing test calls/bodies remain protected. Named upstream analytics implementation files can enter a coordinator scope when supported by diagnostic evidence; raw diagnostic text cannot authorize arbitrary paths. Python acceptance functions and existing TypeScript test calls cannot be changed by the recovery worker. Scope/contract ambiguity that requires changing a product requirement remains blocked.

Upstream feature references resolve through the frozen execution graph. A diagnosis naming the "011 viewer" resolves its registered implementation even without an exact filename. A repair worker can return `RECOVERY_SCOPE_REQUEST` with up to eight exact file paths; the controller admits only tracked source files owned by upstream dependencies, excluding frozen files and future features. At most two scope expansions retain the original checks and consume the same incident budget. An unresolved request stops immediately instead of spending the model ladder in the wrong files. Workers run focused checks; the controller runs the full fixed acceptance separately.

Recovery limits: two incidents per task, six per run, ten model attempts on the existing Luna xhigh (3), Sol 6.1 medium (3), Sol 6.1 xhigh (4) policy; no Astra. Each incident is limited to two hours and consumes the remaining run wall budget across incidents. Provider quota/authentication and unknown/resource authority problems stop with a recorded reason. Progress and incident receipts live in .dag-build/controller-recovery and recovery-current.json.

Verified prerequisite repairs preserve old failure events while starting a fresh bounded worker cycle. A recovery timestamp prevents stale work from replacing the repaired baseline. Same-second checkpoint timestamps cannot supersede a Git salvage snapshot. Publication interrupted by a crash can reconcile a controller-owned receipt against integration HEAD and resume requeue without running repair again.

Validation: 30 shared diagnostic/CLI/process/recovery tests; 16 project recovery, scope, real Git diff and Windows launch/supervisor tests. Tests inject timeout, contract hold, rejected checks/review, frozen-file edits, assertion changes, crashes during publication/requeue, missing-owner requests and model-quota failure. They include passing controls and a real silent subprocess termination. Model accuracy and every possible environment failure are not guaranteed by these deterministic checks.
